Lucent"s General Knowledge
Rise of Magadha
The politicalhistory of India from 6th century BConwards is the hislory
of strugglebetween four states-Magadha Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti-for
supremacy:
Ultimately the kingdom of Magadha emerged to be the most powerful
one and succeeded in founding an empire
Causes of Magadha'$ success
(i) Magadhaenjoyedanadvantageous geographical positionin theage
ofiron; because the richest iron deposits were situated not far away
from Rajgir; the earliest capital Magadha and could be used for
making weapons
(ii) Magadha lay at the centre of the middle Gangetic plain: The
allutiun once cleared of the jungles, proved immense fertile and
food surplus was thus available
(iii) Magadha enjoyed special advantage in military organisation:
Although the Indian states were well acquainted with the use of
horses and chariots, it was Magadha which first used elephants on
large scale in its war against its neighbours_
Haryanaka Dynasty 544 BC-412 BC
Bimbisara (Shronika) 544 BC-492 BC
He was the founder of Haryanka dynasty:
Magadha came into prominence under the leadership of Bimbisara
He was a contemporary of Gautama Buddha_
He married the princesses of Kosala (Kosaldevil Mahakosala-sister of
Kosal King Prasenjit), Lichchhavi (Chellana-sister of Lichchhavi Head
Chetaka) and Madra (Khema-daughter of Madra king) which helped
him in his expansionist policy:
He gained a part of Kashi as the dowry in his marriage with the sister
king Prasenjit of Kosala.
He conquered Anga.
He sent a royal physician, Jivaka to Ujjain, when Avanti King Pradyota
was attacked by jaundice:
Known as Seniya. He was the first Indian king who had regular and
standing ary
He built the city of New Rajagriha_
Ajatashatru (Kunika) 492 BC 460 BC
Bimbisara was succeeded by his son Ajatashatru. Ajatashatru killed his
father and seized the throne:
Ajatashatru followed more aggressive policy He gained complete
control over Kashiand broke the earlier amicable relations by attacking
his maternal uncle Prasenjit; the king of Kosala.
